canonical_claim: The classifier's measured reliability is high on its own corpora -- alpha 0.934 on generated statements and 0.894 on published documents -- and every claim in the specification is labelled by what backs it.
recommended_action: Keep the numbers with their rater count and corpus. An alpha without those is not comparable to anything, and the evidence convention must survive as a key to reading every other claim.
synthesis: The headline numbers and the evidence convention that qualifies them. The numbers are strong against the published comparisons -- argumentative zoning at 0.71 with seven categories, CoreSC at 0.50-0.57 with eleven, this taxonomy at fifteen labels -- but they are model raters measuring reproducibility of one codebook, not agreement with a human gold set. The three-way VERIFIED/MEASURED/DESIGN convention is what makes the rest of the corpus readable, because it separates claims with published backing from claims with in-house backing from claims with none. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.

canonical_claim: The taxonomy is five coarse types and fifteen fine labels with a fixed mapping; four labels are anchored on categories with published agreement figures and eleven are not.
recommended_action: Keep the mapping and the anchors together, with the borrowed-figure qualification attached. Separating them would let the numbers read as measurements of these labels.
synthesis: The structure and the provenance of its reliability claims. The lookup-table property of the mapping is what keeps the coarse tier free of judgment. The anchor figures are borrowed: the kappa quoted is the anchor category's agreement in the cited scheme, not this label's, and eleven of fifteen labels have no anchor at all. A reader who takes the table as fifteen measured labels has misread it, and the specification says so at the point of the table. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.

canonical_claim: Per-category reliability varies twofold within a scheme and the abstract categories are systematically worst, which forces three design rules.
recommended_action: Keep the CoreSC per-category figures with the three rules. The rules are only justified by the spread, and the prediction that was later confirmed is what makes them more than plausible reasoning.
synthesis: The empirical regularity that governs the whole specification, and the three rules it produces: the model coarse type is the known weak point so principle is written as a surface test; anything that cannot be written as a surface test should be expected near 0.45; and per-category agreement must be reported separately. The first rule generated a prediction that was later tested on this codebook and held, which is unusual -- most design rationale in this corpus is never checked.

canonical_claim: The general residual must be assigned by code and cannot be driven by self-reported confidence; abstention rules were measured and every one of them loses.
recommended_action: Keep the threshold table intact and keep the generalization with it. The replacement mechanism -- cross-run disagreement -- is unmeasured and must be marked as such.
synthesis: A design rule with two independent kinds of backing. The published finding is that a named fallback given to a model is catastrophic -- 96.1 per cent agreement with Fleiss kappa -0.001 and the minority class never identified. The in-house finding is that self-reported confidence cannot replace it: argmax over scores holds at 0.930 but every threshold rule loses, down to 0.605 at threshold 90 with 86 per cent falling through. The mechanism is that raters disagree about their own uncertainty more than about the label, which generalizes into the corpus's most transferable claim: anything turning one classification decision into two costs more in the second step than it gains in the first.

canonical_claim: Four labels were removed after the collision test, and the specification separates which removals the data justified from which were editorial.
recommended_action: Keep the removals with their evidence class distinguished. Reporting all four as measured would misstate what the collision test showed.
synthesis: One removal was measured -- conclusion merging into finding, the worst-colliding pair at 11 co-occurrences. Three were editorial: study, permission and tradeoff drew zero assignments, but the specification states plainly that this was an item-set coverage gap and so the test did not show them weak. The two gaps left behind are named, one since closed and one still open, and the merge is criticized in the same breath for widening a label already behaving as a residual at 24 per cent. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.

canonical_claim: Status is a four-rung field on every type; asking for it improves type agreement rather than costing it, and it is dependent on type without collapsing into it.
recommended_action: Keep the ladder definitions in usable form and keep the entropy table, which is the argument for scoping the field that v1 deliberately does not act on.
synthesis: The largest design change in the corpus and the best-evidenced. The ladder reaches alpha 0.896, above the type taxonomy's 0.877 on the same items. The predicted weak boundary -- floated against proposed -- turned out to be the cleanest, at 2 rater-pairs, and the real difficulty is at the top. Asking for status raised type agreement from 0.841 to 0.877, inverting the main risk in the two-field design. Cramer's V of 0.595 puts 51 per cent of status outside what type predicts, and the residual-entropy table shows exactly where it pays: 1.84 bits on dependency, 0.00 on definition. All of it is four raters with no confidence intervals.

canonical_claim: The second collision test's headline gain was confounded by a changed item set, and the control shows the restructure bought approximately nothing.
recommended_action: Keep both the headline and the control. Deleting the retracted claim would remove the corpus's clearest demonstration of how an item-set confound reads.
synthesis: A retraction preserved alongside what it retracts. The headline read fine alpha 0.778 to 0.858 and coarse 0.866 to 0.927; holding items fixed, the taxonomy alone moved +0.009 fine and -0.075 coarse, while the item set alone moved +0.071 and +0.136. The claim that dissolving claim cost nothing was read off an item set containing few of the statements that make it costly. On the other set the cost is 37 rater-pairs between principle and observation. Two fixes shipped in response and the specification states it cannot separate their contributions.

canonical_claim: The third collision test held the item set fixed in both directions and measured +0.096 and +0.072 fine alpha, mostly attributable to two renames.
recommended_action: Keep the per-label figures and the confound. The retention decision for the strip test rests on a judgment, not a measurement, and should read that way.
synthesis: The experiment designed to answer the previous control, run on both earlier item sets so the confound cannot recur. Driver at 0.623 became principle at 0.910; structure at 0.727 became architecture at 0.851. The renames remain confounded with the eleven repaired pointers, which the specification states rather than glossing. The strip test moves its target boundary from 37 to 11 rater-pairs but its aggregate effect is inside the noise floor, and it is retained on the judgment that a cross-coarse boundary matters more than an aggregate.

canonical_claim: Codebook depth and surface-testable definitions dominate label count in determining agreement, though depth alone is not sufficient.
recommended_action: Keep all three, including the third. Without the not-sufficient finding the first two read as a promise that a long codebook guarantees agreement.
synthesis: Three published findings that together justify the length of the definitions section: depth and training moved kappa by 0.15-0.36 on identical documents while growing the label set from 3 to 7 cost only 0.07; concretely-described features reached F1 above 0.60 where interpretive ones fell below 0.30; and a 45-page codebook with a decision tree still yielded only 0.50-0.57. These are separate studies rather than one lineage restated, so the convergence is real -- though the specification's own register notes the reliability literature traces largely to one research lineage. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.

canonical_claim: Every definition must carry a cue, at least two exclusions, and two exemplars, with boundaries factored out into a single separations table.
recommended_action: Keep the required shape as a rule a definition can be checked against, and keep the domain-drift admission attached to it.
synthesis: The required shape, and the anti-drift reason boundaries live outside the definitions: a boundary stated twice can drift between the two entries. The exemplar domains are named as a known mismatch with where the anchor categories were measured, and the specification files that as a weakness in the evidence rather than something the exemplars repair.

canonical_claim: The fifteen fine labels are defined by surface cues with explicit exclusions, plus the strip test that separates the taxonomy's hardest boundary.
recommended_action: Carry every definition's cue and exclusions verbatim in substance. Describing a definition is not carrying it, and this is the content most likely to be lost.
synthesis: This is the codebook. Each definition is a cue plus exclusions written so a rater can check them against the sentence rather than infer intent, which is the property the reliability evidence identifies as decisive. They are complementary rather than convergent -- each defines a different label and none supports another -- and they are useless in summary: a reader who cannot apply the cue cannot classify anything. Several carry their own internal tests, notably the strip test, the breach test, the elevator test and the third-party test, and these are the operative content. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.

canonical_claim: Nineteen pairwise separations bound the labels against each other, several written in response to measured collisions.

Each rule here resolves one boundary and several carry the collision count that prompted them, so a reader can tell which boundaries are known to be hard: principle against observation at 37 rater-pairs, principle against architecture at 17, principle against recommendation at 18, procedure against definition at 15. canonical_claim: The classifier asks one boolean per label and resolves by priority; this measured worse than single choice and is retained only for multi-label output.
recommended_action: Keep the contradiction visible. A version of this that reports the binary-framing evidence without the in-house refutation would recommend a mechanism the corpus measured as worse.
synthesis: The most honest section in the corpus. The published finding is that binary framing beat multiclass by 90 per cent lower odds. The inference to fifteen binary probes was marked as untested, then tested, and it lost: 0.785 against 0.877 fine. Per-test agreement is good and the loss is entirely in resolution -- and the priority order is worse than resolving alphabetically. The mechanism is kept anyway for one property single choice cannot produce: 38 per cent of statements fire two or more tests. The prompt and output-format rules are separately evidenced with large effects: 26-36 points from wording alone, and recall standard deviation from 5.5 to 1.0 when option-ID letters are removed.

canonical_claim: Conversational text classifies materially worse than document text, and three questions about how to handle it returned no evidence at all.
recommended_action: Keep the absence-of-evidence statement as a finding in its own right. It is what makes the chat rules provisional rather than considered.
synthesis: Two published findings and an explicit report of absence. Six frontier models on classroom utterances reached 0.38-0.58 where human experts exceeded 0.90, and few-shot exemplars help model-dependently in both size and sign -- which conflicts directly with a single frozen prompt used across families, a conflict the specification names without resolving. On pronoun resolution, message splitting and context window size, three research angles returned nothing that survived verification, so the operating rules for chat are derived from an absence of evidence. Only one unit from this part of the document appears in this comparison set, so the judgment is on that unit alone.

canonical_claim: The acceptance test is agreement with human labels, not with other models, and a kill criterion is pre-registered against the classifier's own usefulness.
recommended_action: Keep the negative evidence and the kill criterion together and at full strength. A specification that pre-registers its own abandonment condition should not have that condition summarized away.
synthesis: The evaluation plan and the evidence against the enterprise it evaluates. Inter-model agreement is shown twice not to indicate correctness. The strongest direct evidence about typed information is negative and human -- two controlled experiments, n=65 and n=76, both null on task performance -- with a scope limit the verifiers insisted on. No source isolates type labels from linking, extraction or reranking, and the one payoff that replicates across three memory systems is temporal validity rather than typing. The kill criterion follows: run the ablation, refuse preference as a gain, and drop the classifier if no query class improves.
